craft_claim: Sustained abstraction without concrete anchors loses comprehension and retention; philosophical writing must ground each abstract move in a concrete instance and then explicitly fade to the general claim.

supporting_evidence.location: Chapters on dual coding and the concreteness effect
supporting_evidence.note: Dual coding theory holds that concrete content engages both verbal and imaginal systems while abstract content is represented mainly verbally, giving concrete items a recall advantage.
The review supports beginning with a concrete instantiation and explicitly fading toward the abstract representation; immediate abstraction reduces transfer and comprehension.

scope: All forms carrying abstract argument, especially academic, blog and copy where the reader has not chosen dense theory.
exceptions: Expert specialist audiences can tolerate longer abstract runs, but the concreteness effect persists across skill levels; the dose shifts, not the principle.
